title: Slow-Cooker Lamb Shanks
subtitle: Braised lamb shanks in red wine with rosemary and garlic
excerpt: Lamb shanks browned and then cooked in a slow cooker for 8 hours in red wine, tomatoes, stock, and rosemary until the meat is falling from the bone. A restaurant-quality result with very little effort.

recipe.sourceNotes: Braised lamb shanks are one of the great dishes of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cooking, appearing in Greek (arni stifado), Italian (stinco di agnello), and Turkish cuisines. The shank is one of the most flavourful and affordable cuts of lamb: the large amount of connective tissue and bone contributes collagen to the braising liquid, which converts to gelatin during long, slow cooking and creates a rich, self-thickening sauce.

recipeTools.notes: A 5-6 litre slow cooker to fit 4 shanks.

content.text: Brown the shanks all over in a hot pan before they go into the slow cooker: the Maillard reaction flavours from browning are what give the finished dish its depth. The shanks will be cooked well before the liquid reduces to a proper sauce: reduce the braising liquid in a separate pan after the shanks are done.
Season the lamb shanks generously with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large pan over high heat. Brown the shanks on all sides for 8 to 10 minutes in total. Transfer to the slow cooker.

In the same pan, cook the onion, carrot, and garlic for 5 minutes. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the red wine. Boil for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, lamb stock, rosemary, and bay leaves. Pour all of this over the lamb shanks.
Cook on LOW for 8 hours or HIGH for 4 to 5 hours until the meat is tender and pulling away from the bone.

Lift the shanks out carefully. Strain the cooking liquid into a saucepan. Bring to the boil and reduce for 8 to 10 minutes until glossy and lightly thickened. Taste and season. Pour over the shanks. Serve with mashed potato or polenta.
